clue.text: Painter manages to capture one foreign city

indicators.note: to capture something is to hold it within, so the painter's name surrounds the numeral

parts.note: Edvard Munch, the Norwegian painter of The Scream
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An artist succeeds in painting a scene of some city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manages to capture' puts I inside MUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Munich is the Bavarian capital, a city foreign to the British setter.

clue.text: Woman crazy in the morning, beginning to erupt

parts.note: mad means crazy
am stands for ante meridiem, before noon

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word erupt is taken

explanation.surface: A woman goes wild one morning and starts to explode.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame is a title for a woman, French for a married lady.

clue.text: FT pointer could show money made

indicators.note: these letters could be arranged to show another word

explanation.surface: A tip in the Financial Times reveals what money was made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could show' rearranges FT POINTER. The FT is the Financial Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Net profit is the money earned after all costs are deducted.

clue.text: Study journey — see it on a map?

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a tour is a journey

explanation.surface: Planning a trip by looking at the route on a map.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'it' as the answer: a thing seen on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: Contour lines on maps join points of equal height.

clue.text: Shocked, being exposed outside student event

indicators.note: the first piece stands outside the second, wrapping round it

parts.note: to be outed is to have a secret exposed publicly
a rag is a British student charity event, as in rag week

explanation.surface: Someone is scandalised at being unmasked at a university party.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag is a British student fundraising event, often a week of stunts; 'outside' wraps the exposure word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outraged and shocked are synonyms for being deeply offended.

clue.text: Cold man, i.e. no lout becoming excited

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: An aloof man contrasts with a hooligan who gets worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unemotional is cold and detached, showing no feeling.

clue.text: Went around gallery protected by staff

indicators.note: the gallery is guarded within the staff, which surrounds it

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A visitor toured an art gallery watched over by its attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like employees but is a stick; 'protected by' puts the London gallery inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotated means turned or revolved, going round an axis.

clue.text: Composer needs good fortune

parts.note: luck means fortune

explanation.surface: A musician needs a bit of luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Christoph Willibald Gluck was the German composer of Orfeo ed Euridice.

clue.text: Senior ladies performed start of song with inner longing

indicators.note: the longing piece is placed in the interior of the first piece

parts.note: done means performed or carried out
a yen is a longing or craving

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word song

explanation.surface: Elderly women sang the opening of a song full of yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with inner' places the longing in the middle of 'performed', and the song's first letter follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyenne is the most respected senior woman in a field.

clue.text: Indulgent, allowing bit of noise after party

indicators.note: the bit of noise comes after the party in the answer

parts.note: a do is a party or social function
a ting is a short ringing sound

explanation.surface: Someone lenient lets the neighbours make a little racket once the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A doting parent is fondly over-indulgent, lavishing excessive affection.

clue.text: Square contains a flowering plant

indicators.note: the outer word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: a hundred is ten squared, so a square may be a century

explanation.surface: A town square has a flowerbed in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is not a plaza: 100 is the square of 10, so a square can be a century. 'contains' puts A inside CENTURY.
explanation.definitionFit: Centaury is a small pink-flowered herb of the gentian family.

clue.text: Traveller in company game faced with ruin

indicators.note: the ruin piece faces, so stands in front of, the company and game pieces

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman joins a firm only to see its sporting venture go to ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian merchant famed for his journeys to China.

clue.text: Individualists in a state of wickedness?

parts.note: originals are unconventional, one-of-a-kind people

explanation.surface: Are free-thinkers somehow sinful?
explanation.definitionFit: In Christian doctrine humans are born into a sinful condition inherited from Adam's fall.

clue.text: Accepted with thanks by little fellow

parts.note: ta is British informal for thanks
Ken is a short form of the man's name Kenneth

explanation.surface: A small man receives something with gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals a shortened name: KEN is short for Kenneth. TA is everyday British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken can mean received or accepted, as in taken on board.

clue.text: Maybe port is given extra defence before victory against foe finally

parts.note: fortified means strengthened with defensive works
a win is a victory

indicators.note: the final letter of the word foe is used

explanation.surface: A harbour town gets more fortifications ahead of a triumph over the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe port' looks like a harbour; it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Port is an example of a wine strengthened with added brandy, as sherry and madeira are too.

clue.text: Setter-up of home to delay, having hesitation

parts.note: in means at home
to stall is to delay
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A householder procrastinates, umming and erring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter-up' reads as a crossword setter; it is someone who sets things up.
explanation.definitionFit: An installer fits or sets up equipment, so is a setter-up.

clue.text: Strange nude wandering about town freely

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, that is around, the second
these letters wander out of their order

explanation.surface: An odd sight: a naked person roaming loose about the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' makes UNED and 'freely' rearranges the town; 'about' wraps the first round the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwonted means unusual or unaccustomed, hence strange.

clue.text: They want us to take things in properly

definitions.text: They want us to take things in properly

parts.words: They want us to take things in properly
parts.note: sounds like teachers wanting us to absorb lessons, but means experts who want us to ingest food sensibly

explanation.surface: Educators who want pupils to absorb their lessons properly.
explanation.definitionFit: Diet experts advise people on eating well, that is, taking in the right food.

clue.text: This writer's joining chum, because they are beasts

parts.note: the setter speaking of themself: I am, shortened
a pal is a chum
as can mean because

explanation.surface: The writer befriends someone, since they are both animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Impalas are African antelopes, so they are beasts.

clue.text: Plain little son and a very little girl

parts.note: s is the short form of son
v is the abbreviation for very
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A modest boy and a tiny girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals abbreviation: S for son, V for very.
explanation.definitionFit: A savanna is a grassy plain in tropical regions.

clue.text: A boy as an individual

parts.note: per means a, as in five pounds a head
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad viewed as his own person.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a single human being, an individual.

clue.text: Admit personal period of good fortune

parts.note: own means belonging personally to someone
an up is a good spell, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Confessing that one has had a lucky streak.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess or admit a fault, an idiom.

clue.text: Shiny substance with nitrogen put over area of land

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen
an acre is a measure of land area

explanation.surface: A gleaming fertiliser is spread over a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Nacre, or mother-of-pearl, is the iridescent lining of shells.

clue.text: Temper shown when gangster, priest and troublemaker meet

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster
Levi, the biblical patriarch whose descendants the Levites served as priests
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: A short temper flares when a crook, a cleric and a rabble-rouser come together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun meaning anger; it is the verb, to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or ease it, a synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Laughing when touched may be difficult

definitions.meaning: describes someone who giggles when tickled
a tricky, delicate situation needing careful handling

explanation.surface: Someone who giggles at a touch can be hard to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: sensitive to tickling, and awkward or delicate, like a ticklish problem.

clue.text: Germanic folk? They could be obtuse

definitions.meaning: a Germanic people who settled in England, giving it its name
obtuse describes geometric figures greater than ninety degrees

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some German people might be dim-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: The tribe that settled eastern England, and geometric figures that may be acute, right or obtuse.

clue.text: One may provide cover-up after accident

definitions.text: One may provide cover-up after accident

parts.words: One may provide cover-up after accident
parts.note: sounds like hushing up a scandal, but means a covering laid on a wound

explanation.surface: Someone hides the truth after a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandage or gauze pad applied to a wound covers the injury.

clue.text: President making a mark in print

definitions.meaning: a diacritic printed over a vowel to show it is long

explanation.surface: A head of state making an impression in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: The French president shares a name with the bar placed over a long vowel.
